The working file is the complete analysis and the reports are its reader copies — each should be read in full; this message is not the analysis.

In one sentence: adopt a managed identity provider now, scoped to only what 120 tenants and zero enterprise customers actually require (core sessions, password storage/reset, basic org model), deferring MFA depth, audit-log depth, and SSO/SCIM connections until a real deal needs them — confidence MEDIUM, because that rating is capped by several explicitly flagged, verifiable-but-unverified premises (whether an enterprise SSO ask is already live, whether the engineering-time estimates match this team's real velocity, and whether leadership agrees with the trade-off weighting this analysis used).

One framing flaw in the original question is also flagged directly in the analysis: build and buy do not require the same auth feature scope, so comparing them as if they did understates how much the build path would actually need to replicate.
